Equivalent fractions on a number line
That two fractions can sit on exactly the same point of a number line, and that when they do, they are worth the same.
I can mark halves, quarters and eighths on the same line.
I can name two fractions that land on the same point.
I can explain why 1/2 and 4/8 are equal without drawing.

A fraction tells you two things: how many equal parts the whole is cut into (the bottom number), and how many of those parts you are counting (the top number). Cutting a whole into more parts makes each part smaller — so you need more of them to reach the same place.

p.aria-label: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into eighths, with one half marked at the fourth eighth

Cut the line into quarters and mark 3/4. It sits three steps along out of four.
Cut the same line into eighths. Every quarter is now two eighths.
Three quarters is three lots of two eighths, which is six eighths.
Both land on the same point, so 3/4 = 6/8.
adding the same number to the top and the bottom. 3/4 is not 4/5. Equivalent fractions come from multiplying both numbers, not adding to them.
